newsitem.title: ITALY: CYCLING-INJURED TONKOV HITS BACK IN GIRO.
newsitem.headline: CYCLING-INJURED TONKOV HITS BACK IN GIRO.

text.p: Russian Pavel Tonkov dispelled fears about a troublesome knee as he fought for the pink jersey of Giro d'Italia leader Ivan Gotti on Friday.
As they climbed the 10 kilometres to the 1883-metre Passo del Tonale finish of the 176-km 20th stage, Tonkov forced the pace but was held.
The Russian starts Saturday's final day in the Dolomites still 1:32 behind Gotti.
"We were very worried about Pavel," said a team official. "He has a problem with a ligament behind his right knee, but this morning Pavel said he wanted to race."
Tonkov's crash on Thursday left him with a sore shoulder and elbow, but his knee was "the greatest problem. Early in the stage he had some trouble with his knee and elbow, but it cleared".
Gotti, Tonkov, and other contenders arrived more than 10 minutes after Jose Gonzales had given Colombia their first stage success since 1995.
Gotti said: "It was not an easy day because Tonkov is not in such bad shape, but on Saturday the Mortirolo climb should be easier for me because I am lighter.
"I intend to save my energy, and our team will try to control the race. If I see Tonkov is having a hard time on the Mortirolo then I will attack."
The 12.6-km climb follows four other mountains, and has been decisive in past Giro. Last year Gotti was the first to its 1,883-metre summit.

Another with ambitions for victory at Edolo on Saturday is Gonzalez. The tiny Colombian has powered away with the green jersey of best climber, and on Friday he raced clear of his co-leaders in the last 10 kms.
He showed no signs of Thursday's efforts through the Dolomites where he was first to five of the six climbs to strengthen his lead for the 'mountaineering' colours.
This was his first victory of the season, and the seventh Giro stage win for Colombia, a run started by Luis Herrera in 1989.
Gonzalez was in the opening move after five kms when seven escaped. The group grew to nine including 1995 Giro winner Yevgeny Berzin.
Gonzalez said: "I live at 2,600 metres near Boyaca, so the Dolomites suit me. I prepared especially for the Giro and to win a stage."
The Giro ends on Sunday with a race into Milan.
